name: King of the sons of Ammon
overview: The King of the sons of Ammon was a male monarch ruling the Ammonite people during the period of the judges, as noted in Judges 11:12. Scripture identifies him solely by his title without providing additional personal or tribal details. His role situates him within the historical context of Israel's neighboring nations during a time of frequent conflict and leadership transitions.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of the sons of Ammon' literally means 'king [of the] sons [of] Ammon,' indicating his position as the ruler over the Ammonite people. This designation is a title rather than a personal name and was not given by God, reflecting a secular leadership role referenced in Judges 11:12.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for this person beyond his identification as the king of Ammon during the time of the judges. No additional familial or relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of the sons of Ammon holds significance as a representative of the Ammonite nation during the era of the judges, a period marked by Israel's struggles with surrounding peoples. His mention in Judges 11:12 situates him as a key figure in the geopolitical landscape confronting Israel at that time. Though unnamed, his leadership role exemplifies the challenges Israel faced from neighboring kingdoms before the establishment of the monarchy.
